newsitem.title: GERMANY: IMF sees German deficit ratio at 3.3 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees German deficit ratio at 3.3 pct in 97.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Wednesday that it expected Germany's budget deficit to shrink to 3.3 percent of gross domestic product this year from 3.8 percent in 1996.

Although a sharp decline, the ratio would still be above the three percent level mandated by the Maastricht Treaty for joining monetary union and would be above the government's own deficit forecast of a 2.9 percent deficit ratio.
The IMF added that it expected Germany's debt to equal 61.5 percent of GDP this year, also above the Maastricht target of 60.0 percent.
The IMF said its calculation of the debt figure, however, may not be the same as that called for under Maastricht.
The European Commission said this morning that it expected Germany's deficit ratio to hit three percent this year, allowing it to qualify for EMU.
Speaking earlier in the day, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he expected Bonn to meet the Maastricht budget deficit target this year.
